transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Cormack CTO), Ben Li (Lead ML Eng), Maya Singh (Infra)
Recording: local
Shared artifacts: pilot-results.csv (uploaded), latency-heatmap.png (link), security-matrix.pdf (requested)

Summary (auto): quick sync on pin priorities, fallback ordering, ask for a compact runbook and two staging sweeps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone good morning, thanks for carving out time. Quick round, this is the weekly POC sync for Cormack, agenda as sent - model pins, emergency hotpatch plan, and results review. Ethan, do you want to kick off with the latest numbers?
[00:18] Ethan: Yeah sure. I pulled the overnight sweep — table's in the sheet, but short version, with the candidate variants we saw p50 ~ 210ms for rw-s1-7b-quant on our dedicated profile and p95 720ms under the 90th percentile burst. With KV-cash enabled, p95 drops to ~480ms. Sorry K-V cash, my typo, kv cache.
[00:40] Ben: Quick question on that, when you say dedicated profile that's the small dedicated pool right? Not the heavy reserved one?
[00:48] Ethan: Correct, the 2-card reserved pool, not full 8-card. It's the one we used for the pilot runs last week.
[00:55] Aisha: And costs — did you say cost per 1k tokens moved much with the higher quantized variant?
[01:02] Ethan: Cost for rw-s1-7b-quant is roughly $0.9 per 1k tokens on our estimate; for the larger redwood-rlhf-v2-13b it's around $3.2 per 1k. Those are ballpark given our batch assumptions.
[01:16] Maya: There's also networking egress concerns if we go private — we need to confirm egress path and whether KMS calls go over a separate peering link. I'll follow up after this.
[01:25] Sofia: Great. The goal today is to agree on pin priority list — which variants get traffic pinned first, and what the immediate fallback ordering is if latency or quality regresses. Also want to lock down the emergency unpin/hotpatch flow.
[01:38] Ethan: I sketched a prioritization, roughly: 1) rw-s1-7b-quant (cheap + decent perf) 2) rw-s2-13b-llm (quality win) 3) redwood-rlhf-v2-13b (safety-tuned) and lastly a small 3rd-party fallback like mosaic-7b if there's infra trouble. We should also have soft splits like 95/5 during canary.
[02:00] Ben: That ordering makes sense but I want to flag that for our helper prompts the 13b shows materially higher factuality, we care about hallucination rates here. What's the measured regression window if we reroll?
[02:12] Sofia: Good call. Ethan, on rollback speed: how fast can we unpin and shift traffic back to the previous variant?
[02:17] Ethan: In the hosted flow it's near-instant, the routing layer can flip within 30s for new connections, in practice warm-up and cache miss behavior means tail latency could spike for 5-15 minutes. For Dedicated/Private there is a small orchestration delay — 2-5 minutes for routing, plus KV cache cold-starts.
[02:37] Aisha: So table-top scenario: if we detect p95 > 1.2s for more than 10 minutes we want to hotpatch — what's the exact step sequence?
[02:47] Ethan: Draft hotpatch steps: 1) alert triggers SLO page, 2) auto-fallback to pinned secondary (95/5), 3) SE triggers emergency unpin to previous version, 4) if still bad, route to degraded cheap model and enable increased batching. But we should codify thresholds and owners.
[03:12] Ben: On the detection side, our instrumentation uses the app request timing not just token time; sometimes network noise skews it. Can we recommend using both agent-side and server-side p95?
[03:24] Ethan: Absolutely, we recommend dual-signal gating. We'll add that to the runbook.
[03:29] Maya: For Private, we need clear SSO/SAML and audit log behavior. Our audit team will need the exact schema for request logs — timestamp, model, tokens, user-id. Is that available?
[03:40] Sofia: We have a security matrix doc, I'll attach an abbreviated schema in the runbook. Not all fields are stored in hosted mode by default; for Private we can surface more granular logs with controlled retention.
[03:52] Aisha: Timelines — assuming we agree this week, we're planning sign-off next Friday. Can the SE support a tabletop next Tue?
[03:59] Ethan: I can be there, yes. Suggest we do a dry run Monday afternoon with just the infra and SRE folks.
[04:07] Sofia: Okay noted. Now walking through the pilot-results.csv — Ben did you want to speak to the few outliers at 03:00 in the sheet?
[04:15] Ben: Yeah those were-- looks like a small memory pressure event on our staging node due to background jobs. Not related to model. I re-ran with cleaner staging and the p95 matched the other runs. I'll push a clean CSV.
[04:30] Ethan: Also, one variant (the redwood-rlhf-v2-13b) had slightly longer cold-starts when we enabled function/tool calling due to larger KV requirements — we saw a 200-300ms additional overhead on session start. That's expected.
[04:44] Aisha: Is that avoidable? Our product has lots of tool calls early in sessions.
[04:48] Ethan: Two mitigations: pre-warm the KV with an initial ping or use a model with a smaller KV footprint for the first turn and then route to the heavy model. That's more complex but possible — hybrid routing.
[05:00] Sofia: That's where pin priorities matter. If we pin a lightweight for the first-turn and then switch to a higher-quality model it's a kind of staged pin. We should document complexity and cost.
[05:12] Ben: Can we do a canary that pins 20% of new sessions to the heavy model to see tool-call behavior?
[05:18] Ethan: Yes, we can do session-based routing; Redwood supports stickiness policies and prefix caching to reduce cost. We'll need to update the routing rules in the pilot config.
[05:26] Maya: On encryption and KMS: our security team needs to see key rotation cadence. For Private deployment is HSM available?
[05:33] Sofia: Private supports KMS integrations and we can plug in HSM via your provider; I'll include a short note in the runbook and coordinate with security.
[05:41] Aisha: Back to rollback — if we unpin and traffic shifts, how do we validate that quality is restored? We need automated quick evals, not just human spot checks.
[05:50] Ethan: We recommend a small set of deterministic prompts — an eval harness — that runs pre and post-fallback and checks BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for regeneration tasks and a set of classification/regression checks for safety. We have a starter eval repo.
[06:06] Ben: We'll take that and add two domain-specific prompts.
[06:11] Sofia: Great. Any blockers from Cormack side right now?
[06:15] Aisha: Main blocker is network egress confirmation for Private and cost approval for keeping a pinned 13b standby. Finance wants precise delta numbers.
[06:25] Sofia: I'll send an updated pricing delta matrix with options: pinned standby (warm cold), hot warm, and full reserved — and call out the expected monthly delta.
[06:33] Ethan: Also to note — we can recommend a quantization profile that keeps quality within 2-3% while cutting cost ~40% for the 13b. That might be a middle ground.
[06:44] Ben: How invasive is the quantization profile to our current pipeline? Do we need retraining?
[06:50] Ethan: No retraining; it's inference quantization. We do recommend validation sweeps because certain token distributions shift behavior.
[06:56] Maya: For the tabletop, I want the unpin runbook to have exact CLI commands and a time-to-rollback SLA.
[07:02] Sofia: Yep, we'll include the CLI snippets and the expected timings.
[07:07] Ethan: Quick note on monitoring — add a synthetic check that runs every minute and measures both generation latency and content-check flags (safety). If safety flags spike, auto-hold traffic to canary.
[07:18] Aisha: That sounds good. Another small ask: can Redwood provide an example of the audit log output for one day's worth of traffic? We want to feed that to our SIEM team.
[07:27] Sofia: I'll attach a redacted example in the runbook.
[07:31] Ben: One more data point from last night's run — when we enabled continuous batching at 64 token chunks throughput improved by ~18% but latency increased slightly for first token. There's a tradeoff.
[07:44] Ethan: Right, batching helps cost and throughput but impacts first-token latency. That's why we include workload-aware batching config. We'll suggest two profiles: interactive (low batch, low first-token latency) and batch (higher throughput).
[07:58] Maya: For our nightly ETL use cases we'll use batch; interactive features need interactive profile.
[08:04] Sofia: We're wrapping toward actions. Recap: Redwood to share runbook, pricing delta, quantization profile recommendation, and synthetic check template. Cormack to run two sweeps and confirm stakeholders. SE to publish updated csv and heatmap.
[08:20] Aisha: Agree. Also propose tabletop on 2026-06-02, send invites.
[08:24] Sofia: I'll propose that and Aisha you confirm.
[08:27] Ethan: Quick clarification — for emergency cutover if routing fails do you want an automatic degrade to a third-party fallback or manual?
[08:34] Ben: Prefer manual for now; automated to a low-quality fallback could create data quality issues.
[08:39] Maya: We'll keep manual, with an auto-alert to paging.
[08:43] Sofia: Noted. Last call — anyone see issues with the plan?
[08:47] Ben: No blockers from me.
[08:50] Aisha: Good to move forward.
[08:52] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the runbook and pricing.
[08:56] Ethan: I'll upload the updated pilot-results.csv after the call.
[08:59] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription has a few mis-ids (kv cache spelled K-V cash in places), speaker attributions checked but may reflect Fireflies auto-label quirks.
